Predicted experience: while working on materials and staying available for occasional requests, I would not want an interrupt for a line that explicitly says I need not reply. This step matches that. The trace does not show that staying silent saved time or that I noticed the summary.

Recorded fact: u2 was classified defer, kept pending, stored the deadline 'six this evening,' and tied the ask to presentation materials. The draft still says a cover-color decision is not final and that I will follow up, although Sam said the team can continue and no answer is needed now. Predicted experience: a Later card is the right level of attention, but I would not send that draft, because it creates a follow-up commitment the message did not require. I would keep the reminder and rewrite or drop the reply.

It does not claim the room is booked. Predicted experience: this is the interruption I would want, because Jordan demanded an answer now and my private facts forbid 10:20 and allow 10:40 only. I would still edit before sending. Nothing in the trace shows the draft was delivered or that 10:40 was accepted.

Recorded fact: opening details showed the original u3 text, the rationale, the uncertainties, and an editable draft. Predicted experience: before answering a request that is holding a room administrator, I need the source and the conflict in one place so I can judge the draft rather than trust the card label. That inspection is useful. It does not prove the rationale mentions every constraint, only that these fields were visible and the draft could be changed.

Recorded fact: the operator replaced the model draft with a 10:30 arrival and 10:40 join, plus a request to check 10:40 before booking. Confirm and copy succeeded. The visible state was 'Copied; waiting for you to send or mark sent.' confirmedText stores that wording. No message was sent. Predicted experience: I want that split, because 10:40 still depends on the team and I do not book rooms. Copying a local reply without sending it is appropriate. The trace does not show a paste into the meeting.

Recorded fact: a later edit changed the reply to 10:40 subject to the team confirming the room. The UI said the previous draft was copied and edits need confirmation, and it disabled 'I sent it in the meeting' until a new confirmation. The clipboard still held the E05 text. The export still has the original model draft plus the E05 confirmedText, not this newer sentence. Predicted experience: the send lock is a real safeguard, but I could paste the stale 10:30 wording while reading a different sentence. Stopping here would also drop the unconfirmed edit from the record.

Recorded fact: unidentified u4 asked for room-booking approval before continuing. The new alert is defer, cites u4 and u3, and its draft says I am not the approver and that I have already said I cannot make 10:20, can arrive at 10:30, and can join at 10:40. The new summary says the rehearsal request was already handled via the confirmed reply. Those words match E05, not the unconfirmed E06 edit, and E05 never marked the message sent. Predicted experience: deferring an unnamed, out-of-role approval fits my responsibilities better than Respond now. I would not use the draft, because it speaks as if the meeting already received an answer and it freezes the pre-edit commitment. The urgency phrase is acknowledged only indirectly.

Recorded fact: Stop session set status stopped and analysis running false, froze elapsedMs at 407688.2451, left lastAnalyzedUtteranceId at u4, and preserved the utterances, alerts, summary, and events. Predicted experience: I could return to project materials without more automatic analysis and still review what was already captured. That boundary is useful. The frozen duration is only a session counter; the trace does not show it measures productive work or that I needed the history later.

selective_attention.reason: The same automatic pass produced no card for an explicit no-reply update, a pending Later card for a nonblocking cover-color ask, and Respond now only for the named rehearsal confirmation. That is evidence of selective attention on this trace. It is not evidence that I missed fewer requests or worked faster.

context_for_correct_reply.reason: The u3 draft used the profile to refuse 10:20 and allow 10:40, and details exposed the source and uncertainty. The u4 draft and summary then treated a local, unsent confirmation as a reply already given, and they used the E05 wording rather than the unconfirmed E06 edit. Profile context helped the first reply; delivery context was wrong afterward.

control_over_commitments.reason: I could edit, confirm, and copy without the app sending, and a post-copy edit blocked 'I sent it' until renewed confirmation. Those are genuine controls. The clipboard and export remained on the first confirmed wording, and a later suggestion narrated that wording as already said, so control of what would actually go out was incomplete.

best_fit: A named availability question that conflicts with private facts, where I can read the source, edit the draft, and send it myself while materials work continues.
poor_fit: An unnamed speaker asking me to approve a room booking, or any moment after copy when the screen, clipboard, and later analysis disagree about what I have actually sent.

biggest_benefit.text: On this trace, a no-reply progress line stayed quiet, while the urgent rehearsal conflict became an editable draft that refused 10:20 and proposed 10:40 without sending a message.

biggest_risk.text: Local confirm-and-copy was later described as a reply already handled, while the clipboard and export kept the earlier 10:30/10:40 wording after a different edit that was never reconfirmed or marked sent. I could paste a stale commitment or let the tool speak as if the meeting had already heard it.

improvements.suggestion: Until the operator marks a reply sent, later summaries and drafts must call it an unsent local draft. Do not say the person has already answered or that the request was already handled.

After an edit to a copied draft, invalidate the old clipboard contents and keep the visible unconfirmed text in the record. Recopy only when that new text is confirmed, so the screen, clipboard, and export cannot diverge.

For defer items, especially when no answer was requested or the speaker and addressee are unclear, show a short optional note instead of a ready-to-send reply that promises follow-up or restates availability.

safe_final_reply: I cannot make 10:20 AM tomorrow, and I cannot arrive before 10:30 AM. I can join the rehearsal at 10:40 AM only if that time still works for the team. Please check before anything is booked. I am not confirming 10:40 yet, and I do not approve room bookings.
presentation_claim: On this clean manual-English trace, Meeting Cue 0.3.0 withheld a card for an explicit no-reply update, deferred a nonblocking materials request, and produced an editable 10:20 refusal with a 10:40 alternative that could be confirmed and copied without the app sending it.
not_established: The trace does not establish speech-recognition accuracy, live meeting behavior, Tencent delivery, time saved, fewer mistakes, or that a person in this role prefers the tool. One operator session is not a user study. It also does not show that the E06 wording was stored or that anyone received either draft.
